name: Early Childhood Education
description: Foundational years covering nursery and kindergarten. Providers include PCF Sparkletots, NTUC First Campus My First Skool, and MOE Kindergartens. Regulated by the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA).
entry_criteria: Age 3-6. No formal academic criteria. Registration on a first-come, first-served or ballot basis depending on provider. Singaporeans prioritised over PRs and foreigners.
exit_process: No formal exit exam. Children proceed to Primary 1 at age 7.
governing_body: Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) / Ministry of Education (MOE Kindergartens)
key_facts: MOE Kindergartens (MKs) are located in selected primary schools and offer bilingual programmes
KidSTART programme provides extra support for children from low-income families
Anchor operators (PCF, NTUC) receive government subsidies keeping fees low
CDA (Child Development Account) can be used to offset fees
Mandatory Medisave vaccination regime applies to all children

name: Primary School
description: Compulsory education covering English, Mother Tongue, Mathematics, and from P3: Science and Social Studies. Ends with the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE). All Singaporean children must attend a national primary school under the Compulsory Education Act.
entry_criteria: P1 Registration Exercise conducted in July-August the year before entry. Phases 1-3 based on alumni affiliation, sibling links, volunteer parent status, and home-to-school distance. Citizens registered first, then PRs, then foreigners.
exit_process: PSLE taken at the end of P6. Achievement Level (AL) scoring: each subject graded AL1-8, total AL across 4 subjects ranges from 4 (best) to 32 (weakest). Lower total = better placement.
streams: Single stream from 2008; subject-based banding (SBB) from P5 introduced in 2020
key_facts: PSLE AL scoring replaced T-score system from 2021
Each PSLE subject scored AL1 (90+) to AL8 (below 50)
Total PSLE AL score used for Secondary 1 posting (not individual subject scores)
Edusave account provides annual government top-ups for school fees and enrichment
Foundation vs Standard subjects available for weaker students from P5
P1 registration phases: Phase 1 (alumni children), Phase 2A1/2A2 (community ties), Phase 2B (volunteer parents/church), Phase 2C (all remaining), Phase 2C Supplementary, Phase 3 (foreigners)

name: Secondary School — Express Stream
description: The main secondary stream. Students study English, Mother Tongue, Mathematics, Humanities, and Sciences. Culminates in GCE O-Level examinations at the end of Sec 4. Schools may offer the Integrated Programme (IP), skipping O-levels entirely.
entry_criteria: PSLE total AL approximately 4-20. Exact cut-off varies by school. S1 Posting Exercise in December after PSLE results.
exit_process: GCE O-Level examinations (10-point grading, A1 best, F9 fail). Results used for JAE (Joint Admissions Exercise) to JC, Poly, or ITE.
governing_body: Ministry of Education (MOE) / Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board (SEAB)
key_facts: Subject-Based Banding (SBB) allows mixing of Express and Normal Academic subjects from Sec 1
O-Level grade scale: A1=1 pt, A2=2, B3=3, B4=4, C5=5, C6=6, D7=7, E8=8, F9=9
English Language is compulsory and must be passed for most post-secondary options
Affiliation bonus (-2 to L1R5) if applying to affiliated JC after O-levels
CCA involvement important for JAE bonus points (up to -2 for Grade A/B CCA)
Autonomous schools have more flexibility in curriculum and may charge higher fees

name: Secondary School — Normal Academic Stream
duration: 4-5 years (Sec 1-4 for N-levels, optional Sec 5 for O-levels)
description: For students who qualify for the Normal Academic (N(A)) stream. Sit N(A)-Level exams at end of Sec 4. Can proceed to Sec 5 for O-Levels, or enter the Polytechnic Foundation Programme (PFP) directly with good N(A) results.
entry_criteria: PSLE total AL approximately 21-22. Specific AL bands vary by school availability.
exit_process: N(A)-Level exams at Sec 4. Options: (1) Sec 5 → O-Levels → JAE, (2) PFP → Polytechnic, (3) Direct ITE entry with N(A) passes.
key_facts: Polytechnic Foundation Programme (PFP) requires 4 N(A)-level passes including English
PFP is a 1-year bridging programme before entering poly Year 1
Direct Entry Scheme to Polytechnic (DPP) also available for some students
Sec 5 students sit the same O-Level papers as Express Sec 4 students
Subject-Based Banding allows strong N(A) students to take Express-level subjects
With good N(A) results (including English), students may qualify for poly without taking O-Levels

name: Secondary School — Normal Technical Stream
description: Practical, hands-on curriculum with technical subjects like Design & Technology and Food & Consumer Education alongside core academic subjects. Ends with N(T)-Level examinations. Direct pathway to ITE.
exit_process: N(T)-Level exams at Sec 4. Direct entry to ITE NITEC or Higher NITEC programmes.
key_facts: Strong N(T) students may transfer to N(A) stream within first 2 years
ITE direct entry pathway well-established with N(T) passes
Some N(T) students with exceptional results may apply for Polytechnic Foundation Programme
Technical subjects counted in aggregate for ITE entry requirements
Broad-Based Learning (BBL) programme provides additional exposure to technical skills
EAE (Early Admissions Exercise) allows students to get conditional ITE offers before N(T) results

name: Integrated Programme (IP)
description: A through-train programme offered by selected schools. IP students skip the GCE O-Level examination and proceed directly to the final 2 years of their programme, sitting A-Levels, IB, or other qualifications at the end of Year 6. Designed for academically strong students.
entry_criteria: Very competitive. PSLE AL typically ≤ 8 for top IP schools (RI, HCI, SCGS, Nanyang Girls). Some schools use interviews, aptitude tests, or specific subject requirements in addition to PSLE score.
exit_process: GCE A-Levels (most schools), International Baccalaureate (ACS Independent, SJI, SOTA), NUS High Diploma, or other specialised qualifications. Used for university admission.
key_facts: IP students cannot transfer back to O-Level stream easily after Sec 3
Internal school exams replace O-Levels for assessment during the 6 years
School-specific retention/exit policies apply if students underperform
IP is offered at around 17 schools including RI, RGS, HCI, ACSI, SCGS, NJC, VS, Cedar Girls, CHIJ SNGS, Nanyang Girls, Dunman High, River Valley High, SJI, SOTA
IP students applying to same school's JC receive priority in JAE
Some IP students may choose to exit after Sec 4 and take O-Levels as private candidates

name: Junior College (JC)
description: Pre-university education leading to GCE A-Level examinations. Academically rigorous with H1, H2, and H3 subject levels. There are 11 JCs in Singapore. Entry via the Joint Admissions Exercise (JAE) each January.
entry_criteria: O-Level results with net L1R5 ≤ 20 (after bonus points deductions). English Language pass required. JAE application in January after O-Level results (released in January).
exit_process: GCE A-Level examinations at end of JC2. Rank Points calculated for university admission. Maximum 90 rank points.
key_facts: L1R5 = English (L1) + best 5 relevant subjects (R5). Net aggregate = L1R5 minus bonus points
Bonus points: CCA Grade A/B = -2, CCA Grade C = -1, Affiliation = -2 (minimum net = 2)
H1 = 1 principal subject (1 A-Level unit), H2 = 2 units, H3 = advanced university-level content
Typical subject combination: 3 H2 + 1 H1 (contrasting) + H1 Mother Tongue + H1 General Paper
General Paper (GP) or Knowledge & Inquiry (KI) is compulsory
University admission uses best 3 H2 + 1 H1 (excluding GP and MT) for rank point calculation
A-Level grades: A=5 pts (H2), B=4, C=3, D=2, E=1, S=0.5 (H2), U=0
JAE: Students can list up to 12 choices. Posting based on merit and availability

name: Millennia Institute (MI)
description: The only 3-year pre-university institution in Singapore, designed primarily for students from the Normal Academic stream who have passed O-Levels from Sec 5. Offers the same GCE A-Level qualification as JCs. More time given to master the same content.
entry_criteria: O-Level passes from Sec 5 (or Express Sec 4). Specific L1R5 or relevant subject requirements. JAE application in January.
exit_process: GCE A-Level examinations at end of Year 3. Same qualification as JC A-Levels.
key_facts: One of the most accessible pre-university A-Level routes for N(A) students
Same A-Level certificate as JC graduates — no distinction made by universities
Located in Buona Vista, West Singapore
3-year programme provides extra scaffolding for A-Level content
MI graduates are eligible for SNUFA (university admissions) on same basis as JC graduates

name: Polytechnic
description: Applied learning diploma programmes across engineering, IT, business, design, health sciences, and more. 5 polytechnics: Singapore Polytechnic (SP), Temasek Polytechnic (TP), Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP), Ngee Ann Polytechnic (NP), Republic Polytechnic (RP). Entry via JAE after O-Levels or PFP after N(A)-Levels.
entry_criteria: O-Level results with ELR2B2 aggregate (English + L2 + 2 relevant subjects + 2 best). English Language compulsory pass. JAE application in January. PFP route for N(A) students.
exit_process: Diploma awarded upon completion. GPA (0–4.0) used for Direct Admissions Exercise (DAE) to university. Graduates may also work directly.
key_facts: ELR2B2: English (E) + L2 (second language/relevant) + R2 (2 relevant) + B2 (2 best others)
Lower ELR2B2 aggregate = more competitive course
Early Admissions Exercise (EAE) allows students to get conditional poly offers before O-Level results
DAE (Direct Admissions Exercise) allows poly graduates to apply to local universities
Poly graduates can apply via SNUFA in limited numbers or mainly through DAE
GPA of 3.5+ generally needed for competitive university courses via DAE
Advanced Standing: Some poly diploma holders may enter university at Year 2
Poly diplomas recognised by employers; many graduates enter workforce directly

name: Institute of Technical Education (ITE)
description: Practical, industry-focused training leading to NITEC or Higher NITEC qualifications. 3 colleges: ITE College East, ITE College Central, ITE College West. Routes to polytechnic available after Higher NITEC.
entry_criteria: N(T)-Level or N(A)-Level passes. Some courses require O-Level. JAE or EAE (Early Admissions Exercise) application. ITE accepts students across a wide range of academic results.
exit_process: NITEC (2 yr) or Higher NITEC (2 yr after NITEC). Higher NITEC holders can progress to Polytechnic Year 2 via NITEC-to-Poly (N2P) scheme.
key_facts: NITEC to Polytechnic (N2P) progression: Higher NITEC holders can enter Poly Year 2
EAE (Early Admissions Exercise) allows conditional ITE offers before N-Level results
ITE graduates are industry-ready with hands-on training
WSQ (Workforce Skills Qualifications) framework aligns ITE certs with industry needs
ITE International provides overseas training partnerships
Post-ITE SkillsFuture pathways allow continuous upskilling throughout career

name: University (Autonomous Universities)
duration: 3-4 years (some programmes 5 years, e.g. Medicine, Architecture)
description: Degree education at Singapore's 6 Autonomous Universities (AUs): NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT, SUSS. Entry via SNUFA (Scholarships/NUS/NTU/etc University Admissions) for A-Level holders, or DAE (Direct Admissions Exercise) for polytechnic diploma holders.
entry_criteria: A-Level: Rank Points (H2+H1 subjects, max 90). Min rank points vary by course (Medicine ~87-90, Law ~82-88, CS ~78-85, Engineering ~72-82). Poly DAE: GPA typically 3.0-3.9+ depending on course. IB: Points (min 24-45 depending on course). Foreign qualifications also accepted.
exit_process: Bachelor's degree (Honours, Pass, or Merit depending on course). Graduates enter workforce or pursue post-graduate studies.
governing_body: Ministry of Education (MOE) / Individual Autonomous Universities
key_facts: SNUFA application window: March-April for entry in August
DAE application window: February-March for entry in August/October
Rank point calculation: H2 (A=5, B=4, C=3, D=2, E=1, S=0.5) × 2 + H1 (A=2.5, B=2, C=1.5, D=1, E=0.5)
GP/KI and Project Work not counted in rank points
10% of NUS/NTU places reserved for 'exceptional circumstances' — portfolio, interview
SMU uses a different admissions process including interview and essay
SUTD focuses on technology and design; uses own aptitude test
SIT (Singapore Institute of Technology) focuses on applied degrees, often with industry attachments
SUSS (Singapore University of Social Sciences) has a strong part-time/adult learner focus
Some courses require interviews, portfolios, or admissions tests (Medicine, Law, Architecture)

name: Post-Graduate & Lifelong Learning
duration: Masters: 1-2 years; PhD: 3-5 years; Professional certs: varies
description: Post-graduate education and continuous upskilling. Options include Masters degrees, PhDs, professional certifications, SkillsFuture courses, and mid-career conversion programmes. SkillsFuture Singapore provides $500 credit (topped up periodically) for all Singaporeans aged 25+.
entry_criteria: Masters: Bachelor's degree (usually 2nd class honours or above). PhD: Good honours degree or Masters. SkillsFuture: Open to all Singaporeans/PRs 25+.
exit_process: Masters degree, PhD, or professional certificate upon completion. Continuing education is self-directed.
key_facts: Every Singaporean citizen aged 25+ receives S$500 SkillsFuture Credit (topped up over time)
SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP) supports mid-career switches
Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) run by Workforce Singapore (WSG)
IBF (Institute of Banking and Finance) accreditation for finance professionals
Singapore Medical Council (SMC) handles specialist medical training post-degree
NUS, NTU, SMU all offer part-time Masters programmes for working professionals
INSEAD, ESSEC, Chicago Booth have Singapore campuses for MBA programmes
